slots.name: Iron Age
slots.direction: Light cream, not dark ink: every 1880-1930 reading and recording surface track 7 opened is ink on cream, halftones and engravings are ink on paper, and the ground sits 84 dE00 from v1's [T7 s10; SYNTHESIS s5.6]. Palette iron-age-cream-r2: stock #ede3cc (or r2g #e6dec9, Q-P3), ink #1c1712, madder carmine #a1374f once per screen, CVD-built plates (worst group 12.6) [T4 GF2-GF3; C12, C13, C30]. Type is upstream Besley v4 for heads and the one hero figure, Archivo for body, table values, every arrowed string and the Coach card on v1 metrics [C11, C28]; structure comes from measured brass rules not cards, the s11 textures from measured recipes (grain, rule bleed, ink-on-stock duotone), and photos are Tier A only, single-ink under a stock scrim, 4-bit PNG, none on the Coach card [T7 G.2-G.4; T8a H.2-H.7; C24, C25, C27].
angles: THE MANUAL PAGE. Model: the Physical Culture 1908 editorial page and Sandow's 1897 manual body pages [T7 s1, s6.1, s8]. Besley caps section heads sitting on the Oxford rule (card: ruled with shape.rule.head [3,2,1] placed below; sectionHeader: rule), masthead screen headers, stat rows as folio lines between hairlines (statRow: folio), the one hero figure as a challenge line with its unit on the baseline (headline: rule), italic running meta on the web, a dinkus tailpiece as the single ornament. Photos lead: every hero slot the crop rules allow, as halftone plates like a frontispiece. Faces: Besley v4 + Archivo (IA-1).

THE MEASUREMENT FORM. Model: the 1898 Measurement Form, ATF 1912's brass-rule series and the Fairbanks 1919 nameplate [T7 s4, s8; T3 D4]. The app as a ruled record: drawn leaders wherever a name meets a value (listRow/settingsRow/statRow: ledger), caps or web small-caps column heads over a rule, a double rule above totals, stamped nameplates for chips, plate strip and hero figure (chip: stamp, plateStrip: stamp, headline: stamp), a printed calendar (calCell: ruled), underlined fields. Challenge figure in Archivo wdth 62-75 (track 7's alternative; +1 condensed native static). Photos in the fewest, roomiest slots; grain preset 'fresh'. Faces: Besley v4 + Archivo.

THE APPARATUS CATALOGUE. Model: the gymnasium-apparatus and scale catalogues (Spalding c.1891, Sears, Fairbanks 1867/1919) whose engraved profile 'cuts' are the traced icon sources [T8b s1, G3; T7 s7.3]. The engraved icon set is the signature: add tiles as a ruled grid of cuts (addTile: ruled), one traced object (dumbbell, club, rings, expander) as each screen's single ornament, hairline-boxed captions as the period caption idiom, engraved and no-people frames first among photos (gym-naval-academy, gymnase-triat-desbonnet-1911). Faces: Besley v4 + Old Standard TT reading face (IA-2), so the Coach card moves to Old Standard with its own advance table from the native TTF [T5 s5.3; R4.1].
slots.must_differ_from: v1 (graphite, one yellow, rounded bordered cards). Meet Day, its opposite pole: they share only the plate hues and the Coach card's Archivo [T6 s2, s4]. Ledger, which also uses rules and leaders: Iron Age alone owns period faces, thick-thin Oxford rules, caps/small-caps heads, ornament, textures, photos and engraved icons. Chalk and Clear sky, the other light vibes: warm cream stock, never a cool page. The AI cream cluster: stock outside the R3.5 band, no clay accent, no high-contrast Didone display, no CSS sepia(), no faked age, no wood type [R3.5; C13; T7 s9].

slots.name: Chalk
slots.direction: The lineup's one light simple vibe: a cool chalk-white page (#e8ebeb, card #f8fafa, ink #111416), 86 dE00 from v1's ground, where positive polarity helps small labels [T4 R13, s3.2; SYNTHESIS s5.1]. Palette chalk-r2: print-dark plates and mulberry #6c3058, the one accent family that cleared every gate (9.56 from pink-900, 23.3 from its nearest data colour; 0 failures, worst group 13.7) [T4 GF4; C3]. Its distance from the AI look comes from sentence-case labels at 13pt+, a box-score stat line instead of tiles, surfaces told apart by value, and a face that is not Archivo [T1 s0.5, D5-D6; T3 C1]. Web keeps a dark band #111416 under the always-white status text; native sets StatusBar dark with light keyboards and date pickers [T4 s4; prompt s10].
angles: SOFT TECHNICAL SANS (research pick S1-a). Sofia Sans for everything, Sofia Sans Condensed for h1-h3 ('early-twentieth-century technical sans, soft round corners') [T5 s5.1]. Lead card flat at radius 6 (card: flat), groups on the ground with 1px collar separators, statRow: line, kpi: plain, pills kept on chips and segmented controls, knurl input and ghost borders at 3:1. Web 48.8 + 49.7 KB; native SofiaSans-Regular/-Bold/-ExtraBold + SofiaSansCondensed-ExtraBold (picker face SofiaSans-ExtraBold).

PRINTED PLAN, SQUARE (S1-b). Vollkorn ('dark and meaty serifs'), web wght 400-900 at 68.8 KB, native Regular/SemiBold/Bold/ExtraBold, Coach card on Archivo v1 metrics [T5 s5.1]. Square shape tokens throughout: card: plate (radius 2, knurl keyline), btn: square, chip: square, segmented: boxes, field: square, toast: square. The cool ground is what keeps a light serif out of the cream-plus-serif cluster: never drift warm, no clay [T1 N3]. Web headings run 18% wider, check fit at 320. Vollkorn may ship in Chalk or Oxblood, not both.

LEGIBILITY FIRST. Atkinson Hyperlegible Next for text and labels, Archivo for figures, deltas, every arrowed string (the new face lacks arrows) and the Coach card on v1 metrics: two families [T5 s5.1 rank 8; R4.6]. Reason: a chalk-white page in gym glare, labels at 13-14pt 600, the highest label contrast in the lineup. Open shapes: calCell: open, dock: solid, sessionChrome: flat, addTile: flat, no fill on anything but the lead card. Its native statics are unverified and must pass t5-check.mjs and the unique-PostScript-name check before the spec is final [R4.3, R4.5].
slots.must_differ_from: Clear sky, the other cool light vibe: Chalk is near-white with a red-violet accent and keeps v1's boxes; Clear sky is sky-blue, prussian and unboxed. Iron Age (warm cream, serif caps, ruled). v1. Meet Day's paper attempt cards if Meet Day angle 2 wins: they borrow Whiteboard's surfaces, about 1 dE00 from Chalk's (C9) [T4 s3.3]. Never Whiteboard's plum or any warm cream ground.

slots.name: Navy
slots.direction: A dark chromatic ground instead of a stock grey: navy #0a183b with bar #0f223f (navy-r2), clearing all 242 Tailwind v3 defaults (5.19 / 5.09), with warm-white ink and bright re-toned plates, worst group 13.2 [T4 GF5, s3.2; T2 s1 item 5]. The accent is open (Q-P2): pistachio #acdc9c is the checker's proposal, camel #bd977b and old rose #cb7b7e the alternatives, and gold is out because it reads as v1 on blue [C4; T4 GF5]. Overpass, the US highway-sign alphabet, is research's face [T5 s5.1]. Its main risk is sitting only 15 dE00 from v1's ground, so face, accent and label typography must carry the difference [T4 s3.3].
angles: HIGHWAY AT NIGHT (research proposal S2-a). Overpass for everything [T5 s5.1], pistachio #acdc9c (pressed #9bca8b): a pale bright mark on a dark field, the reflective-sign read (judgement). Lead card radius 10, filled, no border (card: flat); groups on the ground; the 'Next week' callout loses its box for a 2pt knurl top border [T1 D4]; bold Overpass heads, labels sentence case 13pt SemiBold. Watch pistachio beside sea-green 'good' (15.9 / 15.3 / 10.9 apart). Native Overpass-Regular/-SemiBold/-Bold/-ExtraBold upstream.

KIT BAG, SQUARED. Overpass with camel #bd977b (13.17 from its nearest default; text 6.53 / 5.96): a quiet, tailored accent (judgement). Square tokens: radius 2 on cards and buttons, card: plate keylined in knurl, chip: square, segmented: boxes. The concept must prove camel reads as an accent at OKLCH C 0.06, or raise its chroma with try.mjs and report the move and every re-checked margin [T4 GF5].

WIDTH-TRUE. Saira, whose width axis the web honours so headings stay exactly in their boxes (h1 0.87xA, load-num 0.94xA) [T5 s5.1], with old rose #cb7b7e (text 5.53 / 5.05 on r2; 17.2 from Club's pink). Native Saira-Regular, Saira-SemiBold, SairaCondensed-ExtraBold, SairaSemiExpanded-ExtraBold from UPSTREAM (google/fonts' condensed dirs carry a 2016 RFN) [SYNTHESIS s5.9]. hhea 1.574 inflates line boxes: state minLh and check the Coach card [R4.9]. Not a scoreboard: Meet Day owns the board.
slots.must_differ_from: v1: the nearest ground in the lineup (15 dE00), so no yellow, gold or amber accent and no Archivo-only spec. Oxblood, the other dark simple: cool chromatic against warm. Clear sky: both blue families, but Navy is dark with a pale accent and the sky is light with a dark accent. Ledger's Club green: both dark chromatic grounds; Navy keeps v1's layout.

slots.name: Oxblood
slots.direction: A warm maroon-black ground (#1a0f11, bar #241518, bone ink #f3ece2) with a cold ice-blue accent #a8d8ff: unlike Navy or v1, its accent 37 dE00 from Navy's and 50 from v1's [T4 s3.2, GF-A G4; SYNTHESIS s5.3]. Palette oxblood is clean on the full v3 list (0 failures, worst group 12.0); if the guard binds Tailwind v4 or pressed states, take rack #1a0b0c, accent #a5d8ff, pressed #97bddc [T4 GF7, GF11]. Schibsted Grotesk, drawn from a newspaper house's printed-media history, is research's face, with Archivo's x-height so the layout holds [T5 s5.1]. The known risk is two blues (accent and data) told apart by lightness only (L* 84 vs 68), so the accent never sits beside back, fat or water as its only cue [T4 s3.2].
angles: NEWSPRINT GROTESK (research pick S3-a). Schibsted Grotesk for everything (web wght 400-900, 47.2 KB; native Regular/SemiBold/Bold/ExtraBold upstream, picker face ExtraBold) [T5 s5.1]. Lead card filled at radius 2, the plate radius; groups parted by space alone; pills only on chips; web headings 1.21xA wider, so check fit at 320.

BELT LEATHER, SERIF (S3-b). Vollkorn on the dark ground, where a serif carries no cream-cluster risk [SYNTHESIS s5.3; T5 s0]; the ground read as oxblood leather, the lifting belt and shoe (judgement, per R3.1). Soft radius 8 flat cards, sentence-case SemiBold serif labels at 13pt, the Coach card on Archivo v1 metrics. Vollkorn may ship in Oxblood or Chalk, not both.

ARCHIVO, RE-CUT. No new family: Archivo set against v1's grain. Heads condensed (web wdth 75; native ArchivoCondensed-Bold from Omnibus-Type upstream, +1 TTF [T6 s3.4]), figures at wdth 100 instead of v1's 108-118, labels sentence case 13pt 600, weight 800 on figures only [T3 A3-A4]. 0 web bytes, coverage exactly as today, Coach card on v1 metrics: the test of whether palette plus label typography alone escape the AI look [T1 s0.5]. Never Meet Day's wdth 62 figures.
slots.must_differ_from: Navy, the other dark simple. Ledger's Club green (grounds 15 apart, both dark chromatic): Oxblood keeps v1's layout and a cold light accent. Iron Age's recorded dark alternative (grounds 6 apart): no period faces or caps heads. v1 (grounds only 8 apart): identity comes from the ice accent and the face, not the ground. Meet Day (no condensed-figure scoreboard look).

slots.name: Ledger
slots.direction: The Ledger: rules, drawn leaders and ranked columns instead of cards, the most complete does-not-look-AI-made device set in the research; its core devices (labels as authored, rules for boxes, bare coloured values, a two-size scale, one colour one meaning) answer the friend's tell directly [T3 s7; SYNTHESIS s5.4]. It sits on club: bottle green #0e1813, bar #15231b, cream ink #f1ead8, pink accent #ffb3c8, the only palette clean on Tailwind v3 and v4 as written (0 failures, worst group 13.6), with one lead surface per tab keeping a fill and radius 4 so it is never broadsheet cosplay [T4 s3.2, GF11; T1 N12, D4; C17]. Research's type is Source Serif 4 (opsz pinned 16) with Alumni Sans heads, Archivo-only the cheap alternative [T5 s5.2; C18; D1-b]. Pink for Rack's audience is Micah's call (Q-P4): the palette may change, the device set is the slot.
angles: THE RECORD BOOK (research pick D1-a). Model: Spalding's Official Base Ball Record 1910 [T3 s4]. Source Serif 4 for text and figures (web opsz 16, 80.0 KB or 57.9 KB at wght 400-800) + Alumni Sans condensed heads (23.8 KB, tabular, has arrows); Coach card moves to Source Serif 4 with an advance table from native statics that are unverified and have no ExtraBold (Q-Q4) [T5 s5.2]. Drawn leaders (listRow/settingsRow/statRow: ledger), bold only the ranked column, hanging date numerals in a 28pt column (D7), week bands where Rack already groups by week (D6), old-style figures in coach sentences only (B6), heads hanging from a 2pt rule (C3). Watch: Source Serif is Source Sans 3's sibling, which is on the Claude-steered list [R4.10].

THE SWISS PROGRAMME (D1-b, extended). Model: The Vignelli Canon and Gerstner's 58-module grid [T3 A1-A4, D1, D8-D9]. Sans only: Archivo for text and figures, heads condensed (native ArchivoCondensed-Bold, +1 TTF), Coach card on v1 metrics, 0 web bytes. Two-size scale 13/17/34/68, weight 800 on figures only, a 2pt rule opening each section and 1/2pt between items, a 108pt label column with values flush left, three-column 108pt grid in place of tiles (statRow: line), flush left ragged right. The furthest of the three from Iron Age.

THE TIMETABLE. Model: the departure board's 'one line per item' and Things' group heads [T3 D2-D3, B1, B7, G3, E2]. Every row one 44pt line; figures decimal-aligned in fixed slots; figure strings in mixed weight (figures 600 chalk, 'x' and middle dots 400 steel; figure strings only, never a sentence); bold mixed-case group heads over a hairline; a line-score total column set apart by a gap and 800; status colour on a few words only. Faces: Alumni Sans figures (condensed, tabular) + Archivo text and Coach card. State the native cost of mixed-weight runs (explicit colour per run, a verify-text-color update) [T3 B7].
slots.must_differ_from: Iron Age, which shares the ruled and leader vocabulary: Ledger is modern and dark, with single rules above heads, never thick-thin or Oxford rules, no caps or small-caps heads, no italic running heads, no ornament, texture, photo or engraved icon. Meet Day: no scoreboard, board strip or inversion accent in a deep slot (C19). Oxblood (dark chromatic ground). Clear sky, the other deep vibe: dense ruled columns against open calm.

slots.name: Clear sky
slots.direction: Clear sky is the calm counterweight to the Ledger's density: one surprise per tab, rows on the ground at a 44pt pitch, separators between groups only, and no boxes except one lead, because on a flat ground Weather-style cards are the tell [T3 s4, s7; T1 D13; SYNTHESIS s5.5]. Palette deep2-sky: sky #b1cfe5, neutral near-white lead #f9fbfc (a 1.57 step), blue-black inks, prussian accent #083366, and the best colour-vision numbers in the lineup (worst group 15.4, 0 failures, red and blue readable on the page itself) [T4 GF6]. Type stays Archivo plus the packaged Archivo Light 300 where a hero numeral is used: 0 web bytes, +1 native TTF, Coach card on v1 metrics [T3 B4; T5 s0]. Whether a sky-blue page suits Rack is Micah's call (Q-P1).
angles: THE NUMERAL (research pick D2-a). Model: Apple Weather's one huge light numeral [T3 B4]. One hero figure per screen at 68-88pt in Archivo Light 300-400 at wdth 100 (the Goal card's rate, Weight's latest, Fuel's kcal, Steps' today, each on its own screen), everything else 34pt or less; scale V 13/17/34/68 [T3 A2]; sectionHeader: plain, listRow: plain, statRow: line, chart: ink. Picker face Archivo Light.

THE LINE. Model: Tufte's sparkline, 'word-sized, with typographic resolution' [T3 G1-G2]. No hero numeral: the data graphic is each block's surprise. Word-sized sparklines beside their figures (kpi: word; 17-22pt tall, 60-90pt wide, 3-4pt end dot, no frame), single-ink 1.5pt strokes with no area wash (chart: ink), bars on a shared origin at every text size, deltas as bare signed text with their arrows [T3 B2]. Figures at text size, 600-800; the lead card holds the tab's one large element to meet R6.9.

THE SPACE. Model: Things' 'clear white piece of paper' and Vignelli's 'white space provides the silence' [T3 A1, D2, E2]. The quietest spec: bold mixed-case group heads over a hairline, no dividers between rows, a grey secondary line under each title, one colour for exactly one meaning per screen, two sizes per block. The one surprise is the lead card itself, stepped off the sky and 3x the next element. It must still redraw every vocabulary block (a deep vibe), not only drop borders.
slots.must_differ_from: Chalk, the other cool light vibe (sky page, no boxes, prussian accent, versus near-white, boxed, mulberry). Ledger (open calm against ruled density). Iron Age (no rules as costume, no serif, no texture, no warm stock). Apple Weather and Fitness: no live-sky imagery, no translucent Weather modules, no rings that read as Activity rings, no copying [T9 C5, K; T3 s4].

slots.name: Meet Day
slots.direction: Meet Day, track 6's pick at 28/30: the platform on competition day, where every motif restyles something already on screen: set index into attempt box, done into a lit lamp, the plate strip into the loading chart, three-tile rows into a board strip, records into the board's current-record cell [T6 s2, s3]. Palette MD-1: scoreboard black #07080a (checker-verified, not the tell hex #0b0b0b), cells #111317, header bands #1d2026, lamp white #f5f0e3, separate good #4be38a, track 4's CVD plates (worst group 14.1); the accent is an inversion, never a hue, needing a declared R2.7 exemption (Q-P5) [C5, C6, C8; T4 GF-B]. Type is Archivo only, pushed to wdth 62-87 for figures and heads, with ArchivoExtraCondensed-ExtraBold and ArchivoCondensed-Bold as its 2 native statics and tnum always on [T6 s3.4]. It may rearrange boxes within a screen, never the dock, and any screen whose rearrangement can't be proven safe falls back to same order, new shapes [prompt s12; T6 s3.9].
angles: THE BOARD. The scoreboard leads and it rearranges the most: every card a panel with a header band on 2px gutters (card: panel, sectionHeader: banner, sheetTitle: band); all five of track 6's rearrangements: three-tile rows into one board strip, rings into 10-cell segmented bars with the '%' text unchanged, a section band merged with its first card's header only where the two strings are identical, Strongest lifts as a scoresheet, and the session's set rows as one board grid down the whole screen [T6 s3.9]. Split-flap seams on hero figures of 32px and up (headline: flap); the dock a board strip with the active cell inverted.

THE SCORE CARD. The attempt card and score card lead [T6 s1.4, s3.6]. Sheets become cool-paper attempt cards (Whiteboard's #fdfdfd / #eef0f0 with its inks, C9): header band, fields on rules, a grid, a total rule. On the board, lists become score-card rows (label, drawn leader, figure) rather than strips; the session reads as a scoresheet. Needs a per-surface palette slot (Q-E3): state the dark fallback for every sheet if the engine has none, and answer the night-brightness question [T6 s5 item 3].

THE LOADING ROOM. The loaded bar and the lamps lead, with the least rearrangement that still passes the silhouette test: the plate strip drawn as the loading chart, heaviest innermost, to scale (plateStrip: loaded), calendar days with edge-on plate slivers (calCell: edge), 12px lamps for done sets and day dots with the current set's box inverted (setRow: attempt), square 6px meters with a lamp tick at the target, rubber-fleck texture on the dock only [T6 s3.5, s3.7]. Rearranges only stat rows into board strips and rings into segmented bars; the natural home of the per-screen fallback.
slots.must_differ_from: Iron Age, its opposite pole and never a remix: no period, serif, photo or ornament [T6 s2, s4]. v1: the black ground is only 4 dE00 from v1's, so identity must come from panels, gutters, inversion, condensed figures and lamps, and it must pass the silhouette test [T4 s3.3; R10b]. Ledger and Clear sky (no deep slot is a scoreboard, C19). The 90s-hardcore gym: no hazard stripes, stencils, slogans, chalk dust, red lamps, three lamps, federation names or logos [T6 s3.10].

notes:
Plan written to /Users/micahflunker/dev/vibes-night/design/PLAN.md. It has the lineup table, 16 cross-slot rules the concept agents work inside, one section per slot (direction, what all three angles keep fixed, the three angles, must-differ, Micah's calls), a self-check and the decisions left to Micah.

The lineup follows research's recommended pick in every slot: iron-age IA-1 cream, chalk S1-a, navy S2-a, oxblood S3-a, ledger D1-a on Club, clear-sky D2-a, meet-day MD-1. I overrode nothing. Every palette named has already been through check.mjs with 0 failures (SYNTHESIS s5.8). The result is 3 light vibes (Iron Age, Chalk, Clear sky) and 5 dark. Picker order: v1, Iron Age, Chalk, Navy, Oxblood, Ledger, Clear sky, Meet Day. I checked with node: every id matches the pattern and is 32 characters or fewer, names are 16 or fewer, feel lines are 28 or fewer, and none contains a middle dot.

Judgement calls to flag:
1. The deep ids name the device set, not the palette (ledger, clear-sky). That way the ids survive if Micah rejects Club's pink (Q-P4) or the sky-blue page (Q-P1).
2. Ledger and Iron Age share the ruled/leader vocabulary. So Ledger's must-differ bans thick-thin/Oxford rules, caps and small-caps heads, italic running heads, ornament, texture and photos. One Ledger angle (Swiss programme) is sans-only, which keeps it furthest from Iron Age. Angle 1 (Source Serif 4) is research's pick, but Source Serif is the sibling of Source Sans 3, which is on the Claude-steered list. I flagged this for the judges.
3. Simple vibes must still define a neutral `spark`. Otherwise iconIn() falls back to v1's sparkle (R8.8/N27). I proposed a shared v1-plus-neutral-spark set as the orchestrator's call.
4. Angle-level font collisions:
   - Vollkorn appears in both Chalk angle 2 and Oxblood angle 2.
   - Archivo condensed statics appear in Oxblood 3, Ledger 2 and Meet Day. Archivo is allowed to be shared.
   - Rule 7 settles a collision: the family goes to the slot whose panel scored it higher, and the other slot takes its runner-up.
5. The feel lines are working copy, written to stay true whichever angle wins, apart from any the panel re-cuts. The "highway at night", "kit bag" and "belt leather" worlds are marked as judgement, not sourced.
6. Unverified files on angle paths:
   - Atkinson Hyperlegible Next native statics (Chalk 3);
   - Source Serif 4 statics (Ledger 1; no ExtraBold);
   - Saira must come from upstream, because the google/fonts condensed dirs carry an RFN (Navy 3).
   Each must pass t5-check.mjs and the PostScript-name check.

Decisions left to Micah: all names and feel lines; Q-P1 through Q-P6; Q-Q1 (caps exceptions); Q-E3 (per-surface palette for Meet Day angle 2); whether simple vibes may name shape-grade looks (VOCAB s9); the simple vibes' spark set; the picker's middle order (Q-M4); and Meet Day's name ("Meet Day" or "Platform").

Refusals: none. Installs: none. Nothing was fetched from the network. The only Bash call was one read-only node -e length and id check. Nothing was edited in either app tree or any worktree; the only file written is design/PLAN.md.
